content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working on a project where we need to read 32-bit signed integer values from an inverter via Modbus TCP. The measurement represents grid production in Watts. The [product_name] module only supports 16-bit integers, which introduces limitations. I’m reading the value over Modbus into VW100 as two words. Currently, since our system doesn’t exceed the INT16 range, I can safely use the upper word, VW102, with no issues. However, for larger installations, values will eventually exceed this limit. Is there a reliable method to convert from INT32 to INT16, perhaps by scaling by 1000 to handle kW instead? Greetings from Denmark :)
From my experience, I haven’t found a way for [product_name] modules to handle 32-bit integer values directly.

If your value is always positive and you only need to display it, you could use an up/down counter. This would work as long as the value stays below 999,999. Anything higher will be capped at that limit.

analysis.insight_summary: Users noted that [product_name] modules are limited to 16-bit integers, making it challenging to process 32-bit signed values from devices such as inverters over Modbus TCP. This means accurate management and display of higher power readings become problematic for larger systems, leading to truncation or loss of precision.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to handle and show 32-bit power measurements by scaling down (e.g., using a gain factor), so [product_name] modules can be used for more extensive systems with readings beyond INT16 limits.
